final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

subtasks.title: Decide: DIY vs hire a trainer for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description: Question 1 of the brief. Determine whether a 14-month rescue border collie mix with hard leash pulling and barking/lunging at other dogs is a reasonable DIY project or needs a professional. Look specifically at: (a) whether reactivity is considered a DIY-appropriate behaviour, (b) what group class vs private training is appropriate for reactive dogs, (c) red flags that mean 'get help now'. Output: a clear recommendation with reasoning, written into this description.

subtasks.title: Find 3 South Bay trainers who take leash-reactive dogs, with real prices
subtasks.description: Question 2 of the brief. Find three positive-reinforcement / force-free trainers or behaviour consultants serving the South Bay (San Jose, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara, Mountain View, Campbell, Los Gatos, Cupertino). Must confirm from their own site: actual price, what the package includes, whether they handle leash reactivity/reactive dogs, and evening/weekend availability. Record name, credentials, price, format, phone/email and URL in this description.

subtasks.title: Build the week-by-week 4-week plan
subtasks.description: Question 3 of the brief. Write a concrete four-week plan the owner can start immediately regardless of whether they hire someone. Must cover: loose-leash walking mechanics, the counter-conditioning protocol for other dogs, distance management, session length/frequency, and what gear to use. Evenings and weekends only. Border collie mix, so include mental work.
